entry.content:
We fixed an issue in the DS-160 Present Work section that blocked submission when “Not Employed” was selected as the Primary Occupation.

Previously, the form incorrectly required hidden employer details, including employer name, address, phone number, and monthly income.

You can now submit this section without entering employer details when “Not Employed” is selected. The “Explain” field remains optional.

This fix covers Fillvisa Free, Fillvisa OS, Fillvisa Plus, and Fillvisa Team.

entry.content:
Fillvisa OS v1.5.0 unlocks all supported immigration forms for everyone, adds four new forms, and improves conditional validation in Form I-485.

All forms are now free

Every supported immigration form is now available on Fillvisa Free and Fillvisa OS, including employment-based forms previously exclusive to Fillvisa Plus.

New forms

  • I-129 — Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker: Prepare employer petitions for temporary workers under classifications including H-1B, L-1, O-1, and others.
  • I-130A — Supplemental Information for Spouse Beneficiary: Provide additional biographical information for a spouse beneficiary of Form I-130.
  • I-129F — Petition for Alien Fiancé(e): Prepare petitions for a foreign national fiancé(e) under the K-1 classification, or a spouse under the K-3 classification in applicable circumstances.
  • I-912 — Request for Fee Waiver: Prepare fee waiver requests directly in your browser, with sections covering means-tested benefits, household income, and financial hardship.

Improved I-485 validation

Updated conditional validation throughout Form I-485 so questions that do not apply to you no longer block form completion or PDF download.

PDF output changes

Removed the hidden meta_formdata field from generated PDFs. This field previously embedded form data as JSON for a planned import feature. Generated PDFs no longer include this embedded data.

entry.content:
We’ve improved validation throughout Form I-485 so questions that don’t apply to you no longer block form completion or PDF download.

  • Follow-up questions now activate only when the relevant answers make them applicable.
  • Improved handling of spouse information - including separated applicants - marriage history, and child details.
  • Preparer and interpreter sections can remain blank when no assistance was used.
  • Inapplicable answers and explanations are cleared automatically, including outdated saved entries, to keep them out of your PDF.
  • Questions that apply to you remain required.

entry.content:
We've unlocked all immigration forms on Fillvisa Free and Fillvisa OS, including previously restricted employment-based forms.

Previously, certain immigration forms were exclusively available through Fillvisa Plus. We've now removed those restrictions, making every supported form accessible to everyone, completely free.

What's Changed?

🟢 Fillvisa Free

  • All supported immigration forms are now free, including employment-based forms.

  • Fill out and download completed forms without a subscription.

  • No account required, no paywalls.

🟢 Fillvisa OS (Open Source)

  • All supported forms are now included in our open-source project.

  • Self-host, customize, and build on Fillvisa under the AGPL-3.0 license.

  • Available on GitHub.

🔵 Fillvisa Plus - Now Focused on Teams

Fillvisa Plus is evolving into a dedicated, white-label workspace for immigration professionals, law firms, and agencies.

Instead of charging for access to forms, Plus now focuses on professional workflows, including:

  • Dedicated team workspaces

  • White-label client portals and custom domains

  • Team and client collaboration

  • Reusable client immigration profiles and cross-form autofill

  • Document management and e-signatures

Why This Change?

We believe access to immigration form-filling tools should be free and open.

Going forward, our model is simple:

Free & Open Source = All forms, free for everyone.

Plus = Professional tools for teams and immigration firms.

We'll continue improving our free and open-source offerings while building better collaboration and workflow tools for immigration professionals.

Get started: Fillvisa Free · Fillvisa OS · Fillvisa Plus

entry.title: Fix: Form I-485 Family-Based Flow Validation and Question Wording Improvements
entry.summary: We shipped a set of fixes to the Form I-485 family-based flow after users reported a few confusing validation and wording issues while completing the form. Some I-485 users were being blocked by fields that did not apply to their situation. The form was requiring…
entry.content:
We shipped a set of fixes to the Form I-485 family-based flow after users reported a few confusing validation and wording issues while completing the form.

What Happened

Some I-485 users were being blocked by fields that did not apply to their situation. The form was requiring passport or travel document details such as passport number, expiration date, and country of issuance, even when the applicant did not need to provide them.

Another issue appeared in Part 4: Additional Info. The employment and education section had two similar fields: “Employer or School” and “Name of Employer, Company, or School.” Because both were required, users had to type into both fields before they could submit the section.

We also found a wording issue in Part 9F, questions 78.a and 78.b. The online form showed 78.a as if it were only asking about unlawful presence after April 1, 1997. The official PDF question is broader: it first asks whether the applicant reentered or attempted to reenter the United States after certain events, then lists 78.a and 78.b as the specific conditions.

Effect of the Problem

These issues could make users answer differently online than they would on the official USCIS PDF.

For applicants whose passport, travel document, or visa details did not apply, the form could feel impossible to complete because it asked for information they did not have.

For Part 4, users were forced to duplicate employment or school information just to pass validation.

For Part 9F, the missing parent question changed the meaning of 78.a and 78.b. A user might answer “Yes” based only on unlawful presence, even though the actual form is asking about reentry or attempted reentry after unlawful presence or removal.

What Was Fixed

Passport and travel document fields in Form I-485 are now optional when they do not apply. Related nonimmigrant visa fields were also reviewed so they do not block submission when left blank for non-applicable cases.

In Part 4, the “Employer or School” helper field is no longer required. The actual “Name of Employer, Company, or School” field remains required, so users still provide the core employment or education information without being forced to duplicate it.

In Part 9F, questions 78.a and 78.b were updated to match the official PDF structure more closely. The shared parent question now appears above both items, and 78.a includes the explanatory unlawful-presence text from the official form.

Conclusion

These updates make Form I-485 clearer, less repetitive, and closer to the official USCIS form language. Users should now be able to complete the family-based I-485 flow without being blocked by non-applicable passport or travel document fields, duplicate employer/school fields, or confusing wording in Part 9F.

entry.title: Fix: I-485 and I-130 validation issues resolved
entry.summary: Received user reports about two form issues affecting Form I-485 and Form I-130. On Form I-485, users were being forced to enter additional dates of birth and A-Numbers even when they only had one date of birth and no A-Number. On Form I-130, users could…
entry.content:
Received user reports about two form issues affecting Form I-485 and Form I-130.

Problem

On Form I-485, users were being forced to enter additional dates of birth and A-Numbers even when they only had one date of birth and no A-Number.

On Form I-130, users could not enter the “Date From” for their current physical address when their mailing address was the same as their physical address.

Effect

For I-485, this blocked users from completing the form accurately. Applicants without another date of birth or A-Number had no valid way to proceed without entering unnecessary placeholder information.

For I-130, users could not provide the required start date for their current address in some address scenarios. This also meant the date could be missed when generating the completed PDF.

Solution

We updated the I-485 validation so optional second date of birth and second A-Number fields are no longer required when left blank. We also corrected the main A-Number validation so it only applies to the actual A-Number field when the user selects “Yes.”

We updated the I-130 address flow so the current physical address “Date From” field remains available after the user answers whether their mailing address is the same as their physical address. The generated PDF now also includes this date correctly.

Conclusion

Users can now complete both forms more naturally:

  • I-485 no longer asks for extra DOB or A-Number details when they do not apply.
  • I-130 now allows users to enter the current address start date even when mailing and physical addresses are the same.

entry.title: Fillvisa OS v1.0.0: Going Open Source, Self-host, and more
entry.summary: Today, we're releasing Fillvisa OS v1.0.0 - the first official release of the open-source edition of Fillvisa. This is an important milestone for us. Fillvisa started with a simple goal: make immigration paperwork more accessible, less frustrating, and easier to understand. Open sourcing Fillvisa is…
entry.content:
Today, we're releasing Fillvisa OS v1.0.0 - the first official release of the open-source edition of Fillvisa.

This is an important milestone for us. Fillvisa started with a simple goal: make immigration paperwork more accessible, less frustrating, and easier to understand. Open sourcing Fillvisa is the next step toward that goal.

We wrote more about why we're taking this direction in Fillvisa is now Open Source.

Introducing Fillvisa OS

Fillvisa OS is the open-source edition of Fillvisa.com.

The source code is now publicly available on GitHub:

github.com/athos2113/fillvisa-os

Fillvisa.com will continue to be the hosted version that anyone can use directly in their browser. Fillvisa OS gives developers, organizations, nonprofits, and technically inclined users another option: run and customize the software themselves.

With Fillvisa OS, you can:

  • Self-host Fillvisa on your own infrastructure.
  • Inspect the source code and understand exactly how the application works.
  • Fork the repository and customize Fillvisa for your own use case.
  • Build on top of Fillvisa instead of starting an immigration-form experience from scratch.
  • Run an independent version while continuing to benefit from future Fillvisa OS releases.

The goal is for Fillvisa.com and Fillvisa OS to complement each other: one provides an immediately accessible hosted experience, while the other provides transparency, control, and the ability to build.

Version 1.0.0

We're calling this release Fillvisa OS v1.0.0.

It's our starting point for treating the open-source project as a first-class Fillvisa product with its own releases and version history.

As Fillvisa OS evolves, we'll publish new versions with improvements, new functionality, fixes, and changes to the underlying project.

You can follow the repository on GitHub for the latest source code:

Fillvisa OS on GitHub →

A New Changelog Tag: Releases

You'll also notice a new tag here on the Fillvisa Changelog:

Releases

The Releases tag will be used exclusively for Fillvisa OS release announcements.

Whenever we ship a notable new version of the open-source project, we'll document it here - starting with v1.0.0.

This also gives each of our changelog tags a clearer purpose.

Releases

Posts about Fillvisa OS releases.

For example:

  • Fillvisa OS v1.0.0
  • Fillvisa OS v1.1.0
  • Major changes between open-source versions
  • Release-specific migration or upgrade information

Added

Something new has been introduced across Fillvisa Free, Fillvisa OS, or Fillvisa Plus.

This can include:

  • New immigration forms
  • New features
  • New workflows
  • New product capabilities

Fixed

We've fixed a bug or problem in Fillvisa Free, Fillvisa OS, or Fillvisa Plus.

These posts will cover fixes that improve reliability and correct unexpected behavior.

Update

We've improved or enhanced something that already exists across Fillvisa Free, Fillvisa OS, or Fillvisa Plus.

This might include:

  • UI improvements
  • Better form experiences
  • Performance improvements
  • Workflow enhancements
  • Changes to existing functionality

Together, these tags should make it much easier to follow what is changing across the Fillvisa ecosystem.

What's Next

v1.0.0 is only the beginning.

By making Fillvisa open source, we're giving developers and organizations a foundation they can inspect, self-host, customize, and build upon.

At the same time, we'll continue improving the hosted Fillvisa products and bringing those improvements back into the broader Fillvisa ecosystem where appropriate.

If you'd like to explore the code, self-host Fillvisa, or simply follow the project as it develops, you can find everything on GitHub:

Explore Fillvisa OS →

Welcome to Fillvisa OS v1.0.0.
